title: Gnocchi di Zucca
subtitle: Butternut squash gnocchi with browned butter and sage
excerpt: Gnocchi di zucca are soft, golden gnocchi made from roasted butternut squash and a small amount of flour and egg. They are sweeter and more fragile than potato gnocchi. They are the autumn gnocchi of Mantua and the Po valley, served with browned butter and sage.
sourceNotes: Squash gnocchi are a classic of Mantua and the lower Po valley, where cucurbita have been grown since the sixteenth century. The Mantuan version is sometimes served with a sweet-sharp mostarda sauce and crushed amaretti, reflecting the sweet-savoury tradition of Mantuan cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The squash can be roasted a day ahead.

content.text: Squash gnocchi are moister and stickier than potato gnocchi and need more chilling to hold their shape. Roast the squash thoroughly to remove as much water as possible. The dough will still be soft -- that is normal. Shape with two wet spoons rather than rolling by hand. Handle gently in the water.

Preheat the oven to 200C. Place {{butternut-squash}} squash halves cut-side down on a baking tray. Roast for 45 minutes until completely soft and slightly collapsed. Scoop out the flesh, mash until smooth, and leave to cool and drain in a sieve for 30 minutes.

Combine the drained squash with {{parmesan}} Parmesan, {{eggs}} egg, {{nutmeg}} nutmeg, and {{salt-table}} salt. Add {{00-flour}} flour and mix to a soft, slightly sticky dough. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Bring a large pan of well-salted water to a boil. Shape the gnocchi with two wet spoons into rough ovals and drop into the water in batches. Cook until they float and have been floating for 30 seconds. Lift with a slotted spoon.
Melt {{unsalted-butter}} butter in a wide pan until golden brown. Add {{sage}} sage leaves and crisp for 30 seconds. Add the gnocchi and toss gently. Serve with more {{parmesan}} Parmesan.

items.symptom: The gnocchi are very soft and hard to handle
items.cause: The squash was not drained long enough after roasting.
items.fix: Squash holds a lot of water. Drain the mashed flesh in a sieve for at least 30 minutes, pressing gently, before adding flour. A well-dried squash needs much less flour and gives a lighter result.

content.text: Squash gnocchi are associated with Mantua, where the sweet, dense cucurbita di Mantova has been grown for four centuries. The Mantuan tradition pairs the gnocchi with mostarda and crushed amaretti for a sweet-savoury effect. This simpler browned butter and sage version is the home-cooking version made across the whole Po valley in October and November.
